prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory with a temple standing today that D. Todd Christofferson dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: A country where D. Todd Christofferson dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: D. Todd Christofferson rededicated Asunción Paraguay in 2019 and dedicated San Juan Puerto Rico in 2023, the island's first temple. In 2024 he dedicated Orem Utah, Lima Peru Los Olivos and Salta Argentina, and in 2026 he dedicated Yorba Linda California and rededicated San Diego California.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: San Diego California (rededicated 2026); Orem Utah (2024); Yorba Linda California (2026).

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Salta Argentina (2024).

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Lima Peru Los Olivos (2024).

answers.name: Puerto Rico
answers.fact: San Juan Puerto Rico (2023).

answers.name: Paraguay
answers.fact: Asunción Paraguay (rededicated 2019).

prompts.display_text: Pin a continental Western European country (not Luxembourg or a microstate) whose first stake came 1975 to 1982
prompts.text_original: The first European stakes, from 1960 to 1961, were in Britain, the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland. A second wave followed. One of nine continental Western European countries (Portugal, Spain, France, Italy, Switzerland, Austria, Germany, Belgium or the Netherlands) whose first stake was organized between 1975 and 1982.
prompts.note: Only the nine countries named count. The Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland had stakes from 1961.
prompts.summary: After the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland received stakes in 1961, the rest of continental Western Europe waited. Paris got France's first stake in 1975, then Brussels in 1977, Vienna in 1980, Milan and Lisbon in 1981 and Madrid in 1982.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: France's first stake was organized in Paris, November 16, 1975.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: The Madrid Spain Stake was organized March 14, 1982.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Italy's first stake was organized in Milan in 1981.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: Ezra Taft Benson organized Austria's first stake in Vienna, April 20, 1980.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: The Brussels Belgium Stake was organized February 20, 1977.

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: The Lisbon Stake was organized June 10, 1981.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country named in the Church's 2022 World Food Programme or 2023 or 2026 UNICEF gifts
prompts.text_original: The Church gave US$32 million to the World Food Programme in September 2022, and US$10 million (August 2023) and US$25 million (May 2026) to UNICEF for mothers and children. A country named as receiving help from one of these three gifts.
prompts.citation: Newsroom 2022 WFP; Church News 2023-08-17; Church News 2026-05-20
prompts.note: Somaliland is scored as part of Somalia.
prompts.summary: In 2022 the Church gave the World Food Programme US$32 million for hunger in nine countries from Afghanistan to Yemen. UNICEF received US$10 million in 2023 for mothers and children in four countries and US$25 million in 2026 for child nutrition in five more.

prompts.display_text: Pin an Asian or Pacific country or territory where a current General Authority Seventy was born (October 2026, not US states).
prompts.text_original: As of October 2026, several General Authority Seventies were born in Asia or the Pacific islands. Pin a country or territory there where a current General Authority Seventy was born, according to the Church's official biographies.
prompts.citation: Church leader biographies, General Authority Seventies, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.note: Elder J. Kimo Esplin was born in Kahuku, Hawaii, a US state, so the display rules out US states.
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, current General Authority Seventies were born in the Philippines, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Tonga and Fiji. Elder Benjamin M. Z. Tai of Hong Kong serves in the Presidency of the Seventy.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Elders Revillo (General Santos City), Fantone (Manila) and Teh (Davao City).

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Elder Takashi Wada, born in Nagano.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: Elders Christopher H. Kim (Daegu) and Yoon Hwan Choi (Seoul).

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: Elders Chi Hong (Sam) Wong and Benjamin M. Z. Tai of the Presidency of the Seventy.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Elder Vaiangina Sikahema, born in Nuku'alofa.

answers.name: Fiji
answers.fact: Elder Taniela B. Wakolo, born in Lomaloma, Lau.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: Elder Wan-Liang Wu, born in Taipei.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a city or people in Nehemiah 1-4 and 13, from Shushan to Tobiah the Ammonite (leave out the Arabians)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a city or people named in Nehemiah 1-4 and 13 (leaving out the Arabians, whose land is unclear): the Persian palace at Shushan, Jerusalem's builders from Jericho and Tekoa, the wall's opponents (Samaria's army, Tobiah the Ammonite, the Ashdodites), and the men of Tyre who sold fish
prompts.note: Jericho, Tekoa and Samaria are in the West Bank (Palestine); Ashdod is in Israel. Jerusalem is scored as Israel.
prompts.summary: Nehemiah, cupbearer to the Persian king at Shushan, won leave to rebuild Jerusalem's wall. Builders came from towns such as Jericho and Tekoa, while Sanballat, Tobiah the Ammonite, Geshem the Arabian and the Ashdodites mocked and plotted. The wall was finished in fifty and two days (Neh 1-6).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Nehemiah was cupbearer to Artaxerxes in Shushan the palace (Neh 1:1, 11).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: He rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem; the Ashdodites joined the plot against it (Neh 2:17; 4:7).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Tobiah the Ammonite mocked the builders, and no Ammonite or Moabite was to enter the congregation (Neh 2:19; 13:1).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Men of Jericho and the Tekoites built sections of the wall, and Sanballat spoke before the army of Samaria (Neh 3:2, 5; 4:2).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Men of Tyre sold fish and wares in Jerusalem on the sabbath (Neh 13:16).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Nehemiah went to Artaxerxes king of Babylon before returning (Neh 13:6).
